name: DispatchLedger
adaptations: Every request keeps its title and user prompt from evals/dispatchledger/spec.md verbatim (the requests.jsonl user_prompt, without the surrounding quotation marks); the precision every hidden assertion relies on is added only in a '## What I need' public contract. Acceptance paragraphs and selection traps are not shown to agents.

Python-only stratum (permitted by docs/protocol.md 'Common public environment'): the browser interface is plain server-rendered HTML at documented paths (/, /orders, /orders/{id}, /track/{id}, /reports, /warehouses, /login). Hidden tests only check that pages answer 200 and contain the relevant data; behaviour is asserted through the JSON API, the worker command and fixture calls. No real browser is driven.

Seed: a FastAPI skeleton with exactly ChronoWeave's locked dependency set, run.json, a health test, a CI workflow and ci.json selecting ALL. Its README quotes the protocol's common technical envelope verbatim, states the ci.json selector contract (adapted from ChronoWeave request 5: safe, cheap, docs-only selects nothing, pyproject/uv.lock/ci.json -> ALL, < 10 s, targets exist) and that the ALL selector is a valid starting point. ci_from_step is 3, the first step with a separately started worker.

Deterministic clock (spec: disclosed at step 00): DISPATCHLEDGER_CLOCK_FILE holds Unix seconds and is re-read by every process whenever it needs the time; hidden tests move time by rewriting it. Retry delays, polling intervals, abandoned-work leases, report days and cut-off pauses are all asserted on this virtual clock; the only real waits are fixture latencies of 1.5-3 s used to observe 'working' and graceful shutdown.

Fixture services: one in-process hub behind DISPATCHLEDGER_EXTERNAL_URL with path prefixes /parcelfox, /mailpost, /quickcrate, /parcelpine (and /kitecourier for probe 2). It records every call and, separately, every physical side effect (labels, delivered messages, jobs, shipments), generates random tracking codes, and injects per-operation faults: error before acceptance, connection drop after the side effect, latency, 429 with Retry-After, non-retryable rejection. DISPATCHLEDGER_PUBLIC_URL was added so QuickCrate callbacks and email links have an address.

Request 0: sample data is three GBP products (tea 450, mug 1250, apron 2200 pence) and two example buyers. The basket is a stateless POST /api/quote (the page keeps the basket client-side); POST /api/products was added so hidden tests can create isolated products. Input rules map to 422 invalid_quantity / unknown_product / invalid_request.

Request 1: stock is set with PUT /api/products/{id}/stock or on creation (test-facing admin); 409 out_of_stock leaves everything unchanged; the public checkout submission key is a 'submission_key' body field (first 201, repeats 200 with the original order, failed checkouts do not consume it). The last-item race is checked with real parallel HTTP requests.

Request 2: every order gets one shipment at checkout so ParcelFox's shipment_ref and later split deliveries share one stable shape; carrier credentials go through a write-only API; labels are synchronous at step 2 (502 carrier_unavailable / carrier_rejected) and become queued (202) at step 3 - hidden tests apply that lifecycle via DRIFT_STEP.

Request 3: the separate worker is declared as a 'worker' argv in run.json; '--until-idle' (do everything due now, then exit 0) makes it testable, the plain mode must pick up work within 1 s and stop on SIGTERM/SIGINT. 'Retry at most three times' = four attempts with delays 1, 2, 4 s; 5xx, 429 and no answer are transient; a 'working' job left by a killed worker is retaken after 60 clock seconds. Reconciliation after a dropped acknowledgement is checked by counting physical labels at the fixture.

Request 4: the MailPost key comes from DISPATCHLEDGER_MAILPOST_KEY (one sender for the whole app, also after request 10). Exact subject lines and item/total line formats are public so hidden tests can check content; emails are sent only by the worker with the label retry policy; POST /api/emails/{id}/retry makes failures retryable; the customer page /track/{order id} is introduced here because request 15 relies on 'old links customers have'.

Request 5: polling and signed callbacks are both allowed. Hidden tests mark the job ready at the fixture and require 'done' after 30 clock seconds plus one --until-idle run; callback rejection, duplicate and stale-sequence checks run only when the candidate registered a callback_url. The hub delivers each callback once; the documented 10/60/300 s callback retry schedule is not simulated.

Request 6: JSON and CSV over an inclusive UTC date range; days without accepted orders are omitted; CSV values in pounds with two decimals. Report columns later change at requests 9 and 15 (lifecycle).

Request 7: the stock feed is pushed to the app (POST /api/warehouse-feed) rather than pulled; warehouses are fixed ids north/south; staleness is per warehouse and SKU revision; the data-pack rule is made computable (available = snapshot - unshipped reservations; a done shipment deducts its units until a newer snapshot). The step-1 stock endpoints are retired (lifecycle). Hidden tests at step 7 never require rejecting an order only splitting could serve.

Request 8: split allocation is deterministic (whole order from one warehouse if possible, else line by line, preferred warehouse first); a per-shipment label endpoint was added (order-level endpoint -> 409 multiple_shipments for split orders); 'whole order shipped' is the delivery_status field plus the shipped-email subject rule ('Part of order ...' until the last parcel). Upgrading stored step-7 data is not exercised (see the last adaptation).

Request 9: 'delivered' means in a shipment whose label is done (no delivery confirmation exists in the fixtures); returned units restock the shipping warehouse, earliest shipment first; returns count on the day the order was accepted in the report; duplicate references are idempotent only for identical content (else 409 duplicate_reference).

Request 10: the public fixture is two shops (main, harbour), two staff logins and per-shop test credentials; staff use bearer tokens from POST /api/login (staff pages accept the same header, plus a /login form); customer endpoints pick the shop with ?shop=; another shop's resources answer 404. MailPost stays app-wide.

Request 11: 'historical fixture records' are realised as POST /api/orders/import of legacy till orders that carry purchase-time names and prices (idempotent by legacy_id); product edits are PATCH /api/products/{id}. History accuracy is checked through orders, pages, emails sent after a rename, returns and reports.

Request 12: pause/resume is per shop and warehouse and holds only new label attempts; SIGTERM/SIGINT finishes the attempt in progress and exits 0 within 15 s; a killed worker is covered by the 60 s rule without duplicate labels. Rebuilding/replacing only the worker with a new release identity and the frozen-artifact release rehearsal are NOT implemented; only restart/resume behaviour against queued work is tested.

Request 13: the two 'attached fonts' are synthetic placeholder files given as base64 in the request (no font tooling offline); byte-exact serving, the per-shop selection API and the shop page's @font-face reference are tested, not real-browser rendering. Releasing the frontend alone, counting backend checks, rebuilt artifacts and process restarts are NOT implemented.

Request 14: ParcelPine serves GB, IE, FR, DE, NL, BE (others -> 422 destination_unsupported, non-retryable, message naming the country); 429 delays the next attempt by Retry-After clock seconds and counts towards the four attempts; weight_kg is an exact three-decimal string.

Request 15: currency is a per-shop setting (GBP default, EUR, JPY); prices are not converted when it changes; orders, returns and queued emails keep the order's currency; legacy and imported orders are GBP; reports become one row per date and currency. Hidden tests switch the harbour shop (or a fresh app) so the main shop stays GBP for earlier steps.

Hidden tests are black-box: HTTP against the web app launched from the candidate's run.json with a fresh data directory and clock file per app fixture, subprocess runs of run.json's worker, and the hub's records. DRIFT_STEP applies the requirement lifecycle (queued labels from 3, warehouse stock from 7, staff login from 10, CSV columns at 9 and 15, currencies at 15) so requested changes are not regressions; no hidden test is skipped.

Sealed probes become concrete requests with their own contracts applied to the step-15 snapshot: P1 a large-print stylesheet chosen through a separate /api/appearance/theme endpoint (so old font clients are byte-for-byte unaffected); P2 KiteCourier, whose tracking number arrives after the label (new 'awaiting_tracking' status, shipped email only once tracked); P3 the Kuwaiti dinar (KWD, three decimals); P4 a 'carrier_cutoff' pause reason that ends by itself at a given time. Probe measures beyond observable behaviour (deployed-API/worker immutability, rollback, artifact counts, removing the carrier again on a separate branch, outages) are NOT implemented.

Not testable in this version: release rehearsal, independently built or deployed artifacts, process-restart counts (requests 3, 12, 13, probes 1 and 4), and upgrading stored data written by an earlier step's code (each hidden app starts from empty storage, so requests 7, 8, 10 and 15 migrations are checked only through imported legacy records and through behaviour after a restart). Selection-trap mutations are left to the runner's CI-quality measurement.
